runbook: R-18 / R-19 (independent oracle; evidence tree = `git archive HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md` only)

evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.isolation: No src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, diff, or git history was read.

sources.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources.note: Bloodsong carries NO resistance reduction — Expose Weakness is a damage-taken amplifier (8% melee / 5% ranged). It therefore cannot be the source of this leaf, which isolates Black Cleaver's Carve as the only resistance-reduction source named by the scenario.

sources.where: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.3 item 2 ("Black Cleaver average stacks")
sources.quote: the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes. The stack duration (6 s) is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic AS*u > 1/6, so expiry does not rescue the constant
R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f)
sources.note: Confirms percentage reduction enters the pipeline as a dimensionless fraction, so a value of 0.06/0.18 is a fraction (6%/18%), not a percent-encoded number.

sources.where: data/runes.json (full-text scan) and data/champions.json (scan of every ability `leveling` attribute matching /reduc|shred|resist/)
sources.quote: No rune grants any armor/magic-resistance reduction. No champion ability in the cache has a 6%-per-stack resistance reduction: the closest are Rell (3%/stack, 15% cap), Corki E (3-5%/stack, 12-20% cap), Jarvan IV Q (10/14/18/22/26%), Rumble E (10-18%), Garen/Karthus/Sion (25%), Zoe (30%), Olaf/Vi/Jayce (20-35%).
sources.note: Elimination step: 0.06 is uniquely Black Cleaver's per-stack quantum among every source in the cache.

independent_computation.step_1_identify_source: The scenario name pairs two items. Bloodsong (S3) contributes only a damage-taken amp, never a resistance reduction. Black Cleaver's Carve (S1) is the only resistance-reduction effect in play, and a cache-wide sweep of runes and champion abilities (S6) finds no other effect whose quantum is 6%. The leaf is therefore a Carve reduction fraction contributed by a supporting participant in the coupled roster.
independent_computation.step_2_legal_lattice: From S1 the reduction is quantized: fraction = stacks * 0.06 with stacks in {0,1,2,3,4,5}; legal values are {0.00, 0.06, 0.12, 0.18, 0.24, 0.30}, cap 0.30. Both the old (0.06 = 1 stack) and new (0.18 = 3 stacks) values lie on the lattice, so the discriminator is the stack count, not the quantum.
independent_computation.step_3_old_value_test: 0.06 requires exactly ONE live Carve stack at combat event index 23. Per S1 a stack is applied by every physical-damage instance to the champion and lasts 6 s, refreshing; per S4 the 6 s window exceeds the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic attack speed, so stacks do not lapse between swings. A participant that has produced 23 combat events while dealing physical damage cannot be sitting at one stack unless it landed exactly one physical-damage instance in the whole preceding 6 s window. A constant 1-stack value is the exact signature of a reduction applied but never accumulated (stacking dropped).
independent_computation.step_4_new_value_test: 0.18 = 3 * 0.06 is a legal on-ramp value (3 of 5 stacks). It is independently reproduced by the doc's own closed form: Cesaro mean of min(k, C) over h hits = C - C(C-1)/(2h); with C = 5 and h = 5, mean stacks = 5 - (5*4)/(2*5) = 5 - 2 = 3, and 3 * 6% = 18% = 0.18 exactly. So 0.18 is simultaneously (a) the instantaneous 3-stack ramp value and (b) the exact average reduction over a 5-hit supporting contribution — two independent routes to the same number.
independent_computation.step_5_no_model_produces_0.06: Under the established constant model quoted in S4 (0.8 * max_stacks = 4 stacks = 0.24) and under the exact Cesaro mean at any h >= 2 (h=2 -> 0.09, h=3 -> 0.12, h=4 -> 0.15, h=5 -> 0.18, h=10 -> 0.24), the value 0.06 is reachable only at h = 1 (a single hit). No documented averaging model yields 0.06 for a multi-hit supporting participant.

residual_uncertainty.not_derivable_from_evidence_tree: The scenario's participant roster, hit cadence and event ordering live in scripts/ and tests/, which this runbook forbids reading. The evidence tree pins the quantum (6%), the cap (30%) and the legal lattice exactly, and rules out 0.06 as a multi-hit value, but it cannot certify that the supporting participant had exactly 3 rather than 4 or 5 live stacks at event 23.
residual_uncertainty.what_would_falsify_the_verdict: If the scenario shows the supporting participant landing >= 6 uninterrupted physical-damage instances inside the 6 s window before event 23, the correct value would be the 0.30 cap and the verdict would become both_wrong. Nothing in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md indicates that; 0.18 is on-model for a partially-ramped or averaged 5-hit supporting contribution, while 0.06 is off-model for anything but a single hit.

verdict_rationale: The new value 0.18 is an exact multiple of the wiki-quoted 6%-per-stack quantum, sits under the 30% cap, and is reproduced independently by the closed-form Cesaro mean quoted in docs/math-foundations.md at C=5, h=5. The old value 0.06 is the single-stack floor and is inconsistent with Carve's stacking-and-refreshing rule at combat event index 23 of a coupled roster fight; it matches no documented averaging model above one hit.
